info.title: Jamf Security Cloud API Reference Documentation: Risk

post.description: Endpoint for generating expiring JWT token. Token can be used for requests against Jamf Security API

parameters.name: authorization
parameters.description: Basic auth header containing base64 hash of clientId and clientSecret. Hash is calculated from string pair "clientId:clientSecret"

200.description: A response containing expiring JWT token that can be used for requests against Jamf Security API

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

403.description: Access denied - can be due to wrong combination  of clientId and clientSecret, request path, method

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

429.description: A response indicates the client has sent too many requests within given time period

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Milliseconds.description: The time (in ms) after which client should retry his request against Jamf Security API once it hits rate limit restriction

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

get.description: Endpoint for retrieving device status information of all devices which belong to Jamf Security account. Successful response payload from this endpoint is controlled by configuration in Radar (details described below). Configuration change is effective immediately for all new generated JWT tokens.

parameters.name: authorization
parameters.description: Bearer auth header containing expiring JWT token obtained from login endpoint

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number indexed from zero

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of records to be returned

200.description: A response containing list of account's devices info with additional pagination information. When 'Show User and Device Information' configuration in Radar is disabled, PII fields will not be present in the response (whole user section, device name)

put.description: Endpoint for overriding the device risk as calculated by Jamf Security.

parameters.name: authorization
parameters.description: Bearer auth header containing expiring JWT token obtained from login endpoint

requestBody.description: JSON body of a risk override request. MANUAL source overrides calculated device risk, whereas Jamf Security source sets the device risk back to the calculated one.

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

403.description: Access denied - can be due to invalid JWT, request path, method

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

429.description: A response indicates the client has sent too many requests within given time period

Content-Length.description: The size of entity body in bytes

X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Milliseconds.description: The time (in ms) after which client should retry his request against Risk API once it hits rate limit restriction

Date.description: The date and time the message was sent

guid.description: Id of device in the system

risk.description: The risk level to be set for the device

source.description: The source of the risk level. This can be either 'MANUAL' when setting an override or 'WANDERA' when reverting back to the Jamf Security calculation.

deviceIds.description: List of identifiers of the devices to be updated
